name: Lactitol

overview.mechanism: Draws water into the intestine by an osmotic effect, producing a colonic laxative effect; systemic absorption is minimal.
uses: Chronic idiopathic constipation in adults (US PIZENSY indication); confirm indications for the local product.

paragraphs.text: The FDA approval label describes a 594-patient placebo-controlled efficacy analysis. The prespecified complete spontaneous bowel-movement responder rate over the first 12 weeks was 25% with lactitol versus 13% with placebo (difference 12 percentage points; 95% CI 6.0–18.5). This was symptomatic constipation treatment, not a renal-outcome study.

A separate four-week randomized study in 172 constipated Indian adults found that lactitol, psyllium, their combination and placebo all improved bowel-movement frequency, with no significant difference from placebo. Differences in populations, interventions and endpoints matter when comparing trials.

The US label contraindicates use in known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction and galactosemia. Flatulence, diarrhea and abdominal distension were among common adverse reactions. Persistent loose stools warrant stopping treatment and contacting the clinician.

The label directs separating other oral medicines by at least two hours because their absorption may be reduced. It provides no dedicated renal-impairment or dialysis dosing section. Minimal absorption should not be interpreted as proof of a studied dialysis regimen.
